newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-RIGA SHIPYARD SEES 1-2 MLN LATS 1997 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-RIGA SHIPYARD SEES 1-2 MLN LATS 1997 PROFIT.

text.p: Riga Shipyard, first quoted on the bourse's official list today, said on Monday it plans a 1997 profit of one to two mln lats and may pay dividends in 1998.
"This year our balance sheet profit will come to one to two million lats," Erik Kazha, company chairman, told a news conference.
"We will definitely pay dividends next year," Kazha said.
He added, however, that it will depend on the market condition and the demand for investment.
"If we will have to choose between paying dividends and buying equipment which would boost our turnover, we will opt for the latter," Kazha said.
"We expect to increase our turnover by 10 to 20 percent this year," Kazha said.
"In 1997 we will start working at a normal pace after the banking crises, restructuring and privatisation," Kazha said.
Riga Shipyard is currently investing in metal cutting technology necessary to build smaller-size vessels.
Total investment could come to two million dollars, Kazha said.
The company expects more orders from Norway if it is succesful in building a small-size shipping trawler this year, worth some $400,000, he added.
"This may affect our 1998 turnover," Kazha said.
The company said that it has a busy repair calender this summer and is working in two shifts to meet demand.
